summary: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Goshen College (1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1978–1984), and she became Professor Emerita at Emory University, where she held a post from circa 1990.

Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Wu earned a PhD from Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012) and held a postdoctoral position at the University of Tokyo (attested 2014).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She taught at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III, the University of Lille, and became a professor at EPHE in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell College, Florida State, Columbia, and Walden University, she taught at several institutions before joining Naropa University in 1977, where she is Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. Ahn held posts at the University of Michigan, attested in 2004 and as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies in 2019.

Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies, art history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, Rhi became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe works in philosophy. Tanabe was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who attended Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held chairs at the Collège de France (1936–1951) and the University of Paris (circa 1937–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Levinson completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins in 1994 and held an assistant professorship in religion at Hamline University, attested in 1996.

Jules Michelet was a historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served as a section head at the Archives Nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who earned his PhD from Kiel University. He taught at INALCO, the University of Paris, and the Collège de France, where he was a professor from 1874 to 1905.

Julia A. B. Hegewald is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (BA and PhD), the University of Oxford (MA), and completed her habilitation at RWTH Aachen University between 1998 and 2008.

Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her doctorate from Australian National University. After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became Professor of Religion, Philosophy, and East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University, and she joined the faculty of Ohio State University circa 1987.
Julia Leslie was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. She founded and held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1992 to 2004.

Julian Schott is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Schott is attested in 2026 as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg and as a faculty member at the University of Vienna.

Juliane Schober works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University, attested in 1997 and 2007.

Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University, attested in 2011.
Julius Dutoit was a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn, studying with the latter from circa 1898 to 1902.
